stem: Who presented the Bihar Budget 2024-25 in the State Assembly ?
expl: On 13 February, 2024, the State Budget for the financial year 2024–25 was presented in the Bihar Legislative Assembly by the Deputy Chief Minister of Bihar and the then Finance Minister, Samrat Choudhary. The State Budget for the year 2025–26 was also presented by him on 3 March, 2025.

stem: Which of the following statements is/are correct about Bihar's economic performance in 2023-24?

options.label: a
options.text: Bihar's per capita GSDP at current prices increased by 12.8% in 2023 24 over the previous year.

options.label: b
options.text: The estimated share of the tertiary sector in Bihar's GSVA (constant prices) in 2023-24 was 58.6%.

options.label: c
options.text: The Gross Fixed Capital Formation (GFCF) formed 4.6% of GSDP at current prices in 2023-24.

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above.

expl: According to the Bihar Economic Survey 2024–25, in 2023–24 Bihar’s per capita GSDP at current prices increased by 12.8 percent over the previous year to approximately `66,828. At constant prices (2011–12), the estimated share of the tertiary (service) sector in Bihar’s Gross State Value Added for 2023–24 was 58.6 percent. Gross Fixed Capital Formation at current prices increased from 1.6 percent of GSDP in 2019–20 to 4.6 percent of GSDP in 2023–24.

stem: How is the fiscal deficit estimated in Bihar during 2021- 22?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: According to the Budget Estimates for 2021–22, the fiscal deficit of Bihar was estimated at `22,510.78 crore. In the Budget Estimates for 2025–26, the fiscal deficit is estimated at `32,718.30 crore, which is 2.98 percent of the Gross State Domestic Product. Therefore, the nearest correct answer is option (a).

stem: Which sector received the highest allocation in the Bihar Budget 2024-25 ?
expl: In the Bihar State Budget 2024–25, the Education Department received the highest allocation. In the year 2024–25, a budget of `52,639.03 crore was proposed for the Education Department. In the Bihar Budget 2025–26 as well, the Education Department received the highest allocation of `60,964.87 crore. After that, `20,035.80 crore was allocated for the Health Department.

stem: Taking 2011–12 as the base year, what was Bihar’s per capita Net State Domestic Product at current prices for the financial year 2022–23?
expl: At the time of the question, option (a) was the correct answer. However, according to the Economic Survey 2024–25, for the financial year 2022–23, Bihar’s per capita Net State Domestic Product (Per Capita Net State Domestic Product) at current prices (2011–12 series) was `53,478. For the financial year 2021–22, it was recorded at `47,296. During this period, in terms of per capita NSDP, Bihar was at the lowest position among all the States/Union Territories of the country.

stem: The per capita Net State Domestic Product at constant prices for Bihar is less than that of the country. In the year 2018-19, it was

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: According to the Bihar Economic Survey 2019–20, Bihar’s per capita Net State Domestic Product at constant prices in the year 2018–19 was `30,617, whereas at the national level it was `92,565. Thus, Bihar’s per capita income was 33.1 percent of the national average, which is close to option (d). According to the Bihar Economic Survey 2024–25, in the year 2023–24 (Q), at constant prices (2011–12), Bihar’s per capita Net State Domestic Product was `32,174, which is only 30.14 percent of the national average of `1,06,744.

stem: The 60.2 percent share in GSDP of Bihar in 2019-20 was that of
expl: At the time of the question, option (a) was the correct answer. According to the Bihar Economic Survey 2024–25, in the year 2023–24 (Quick), at constant prices (2011–12), the contribution of the tertiary sector (service sector) to Bihar’s GSVA was 58.6 percent.

stem: The contribution of agricultural and allied sectors to the Gross State Value Added (GSVA) of Bihar state was _____ in the financial year 2017-18.

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: At constant prices (2011–12), the share of agriculture and allied sectors in Bihar’s Gross State Value Added in the year 2017–18 was 21 percent (21.5 percent according to the Bihar Economic Survey 2024–25). According to the Bihar Economic Survey 2024–25, in the years 2021–22, 2022–23 (P) and 2023–24 (Q), at constant prices (2011–12), the share of agriculture and allied sectors in Gross State Value Added (GSVA) was 21.1 percent, 20.2 percent and 19.5 percent, respectively.

stem: What was the growth rate of the Bihar economy at constant prices in the year 2018-19?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The growth rate of Bihar’s economy at constant prices in the year 2018–19 was 10.53 percent (10.9 percent according to the Bihar Economic Survey 2024–25). According to the Bihar Economic Survey 2024–25, for the years 2022–23 (estimate) and 2023–24 (Quick estimate), Bihar’s economic growth rate is estimated at 9.8 percent and 9.2 percent, respectively.

stem: The fiscal deficit is expected to be of GSDP of Bihar for the financial year 2022-23.

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: According to the Bihar Budget Estimates, 2022–23, for the financial year 2022–23 the fiscal deficit (`25,885.10 crore) was about 3.47 percent of Bihar’s GSDP (`7,45,310 crore). In the Bihar Budget 2025–26, it is estimated at 2.98 percent of the GSDP (`10,97,264 crore).

stem: Which state has the lowest per capita income in India at the current prices?
expl: As per the time reference of the question and the Economic Survey 2024–25, option (a) is also the correct answer. According to the Bihar Economic Survey 2024–25, at constant prices (2011–12) Bihar’s per capita income in 2023–24 (Q) and 2022–23 (P) was `36,333 and `33,763 respectively (per capita GSDP). During the same period, at current prices it was `66,828 and `59,244 respectively.

stem: When did Bihar State introduce the Green Budget for the first time ?
expl: Bihar presented the Green Budget for the first time in the financial year 2020–21. Bihar is the first state in the country to present a separate Green Budget with the objective of aligning government expenditure with environmental considerations.

stem: What is the percentage of population in Bihar State employed in the agriculture sector in 2017-18?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Agriculture is the backbone of Bihar’s economy, in which more than 75 percent of the state’s population is engaged. According to the Bihar Economic Survey 2024–25, in 2017–18 the share of agriculture, livestock, forestry and fisheries in employment in Bihar was 45.1 percent, which increased to 54.2 percent in 2023–24 (Quick/Provisional).

stem: The growth rate of the tertiary sector in Bihar during the year 2017-18 was :

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: According to the Bihar Economic Survey 2018–19, during 2017–18 the growth rate of the tertiary sector in Bihar at constant (2011–12) prices and current prices was 14.6 percent and 17.9 percent respectively. During the same period, the growth rates of the primary sector at constant (2011–12) prices and current prices were 1.4 percent and 6.1 percent respectively, and for the secondary sector they were 2.5 percent and 4.1 percent respectively. According to the Bihar Economic Survey 2024–25, in 2023–24 (Q) the estimated growth rates at constant prices for the primary, secondary and tertiary sectors are 5.7 percent, 8.2 percent and 10.8 percent respectively.

stem: The Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) of Bihar at current prices in the year 2017-18 was :

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: According to Bihar Economic Survey, 2018-19, the Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) of Bihar State at current and constant (2011-12) prices was Rs 4,87,628 crore and Rs 3,61,504 crore respectively in the year 2017-18 (Rs 468746 crore and Rs 344028 crore respectively as per Bihar Economic Survey, 2024-25), whereas as per Bihar Economic Survey, 2024-25, the Gross State Domestic Product of Bihar at constant (2011-12) and current prices is estimated to be Rs 854429 crore and Rs 464540 crore respectively in 2023-24 (Q).

stem: What was the economic growth rate of the State of Bihar during the year 2016-17?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: According to the 12th Economic Survey Report of Bihar, the state's Gross Domestic Growth rate increased to 10.3 percent in 2016-17 [13.3 percent and 7.5 percent at current and constant prices (2011-12), respectively, as per Bihar Economic Survey 2024-25] from 7.5 percent during 2015- 16 [8.4 percent and 6.1 percent at current and constant prices (2011-12), respectively, as per Bihar Economic Survey 2024-25]. According to Bihar Economic Survey 2024-25, it is estimated to grow at 14.5 percent and 9.2 percent at current and constant prices (2011-12), respectively, during 2023-24 (Q).

stem: In Bihar which sector recorded the highest growth during 2005-06 to 2014-15 ?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: In Bihar, during 2005-06 to 2014-15, the registered manufacturing sector recorded the highest average annual growth rate. In 2023-24, the three major activities that recorded high economic growth were Hotels and Restaurants (29.1%), Mining (21.1%), and Storage (18.3%).

stem: The reason for the maximum number of people below the poverty line in the state of Bihar is:
expl: Bihar is one of the poorest states in India. The main reason for poverty in Bihar has been the failure of land reforms in the state. The cause of this failure has been the lack of political will. Further, being an industrially backward state, Bihar also has a comparatively large labour force. Therefore, all the above three options are major reasons for Bihar’s backwardness and the resulting poverty.

stem: The Planning Commission estimated the following percentage of Below Poverty Line (BPL) for Bihar in 1993-94—
expl: On the Lakdawala formula, the percentage of people below the poverty line for Bihar in 1993-94 was estimated at 54.96. In 2004-05, the percentage of poverty in Bihar was 41.4. On the Suresh Tendulkar formula, poverty was 54.4 percent in 2004-05 and 33.7 percent in 2011-12. During 2019-21, poverty in Bihar was 33.76 percent.

stem:
Bihar Government has introduced the Comprehensive Financial Management System (CFMS) on 1st April,
2019. This system

options.label: a
options.text: Will make all financial activities in the State online and paperless

options.label: b
options.text: Will solve the problem of NPA of banks

options.label: c
options.text: Will ensure effective implementation of State projects

options.label: d
options.text: Will manage state government finances including local bodies

options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The Comprehensive Financial Management System (CFMS) was started in Bihar to strengthen public financial management, digitize related work, promote electronic transactions, and ensure a single, reliable source of data. The system provides effective financial control, tracking, and reliability in reporting within the regulatory and institutional framework. stem: What is the estimated percentage increase in surplus revenue in Bihar in 2018-19 as compared to 2017-18?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: According to the Bihar Economic Review, 2019–20, Bihar has been maintaining a continuous revenue surplus since 2004–05. In 2018–19, the revenue surplus was 1.34 percent of the Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP). The revenue surplus kept increasing continuously up to 2014–15, and thereafter increased by 153 percent to reach `14,823 crore in 2017–18. However, in 2018–19, it declined by 52.5 percent and stood at `6,897 crore. In the state’s budget estimate for 2019–20, the revenue surplus was estimated at `21,517 crore. In 2025–26 (budget estimate), the revenue surplus is estimated to be `8,831.18 crore (0.80% of GSDP).

stem: According to PLFS 2023-24, which of the following statements best describes the nature of employment among women in Bihar?

options.label: a
options.text: M ost women are employed in formal, regular wage jobs.

options.label: b
options.text: The majority of women are self-employed, often serving as helpers in household enterprises.

options.label: c
options.text: Majority of women were engaged in the secondary sector

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: According to the Bihar Economic Survey, 2024–25, the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) classifies employment into three major categories—self-employed, regular wage/ salaried, and casual labour. Analyses based on PLFS 2023–24 indicate that the largest share of working women in Bihar falls under the self-employed category. On the basis of PLFS 2023–24, under the Current Weekly Status (CWS), 83.7 percent of total female workers in Bihar are self-employed, 10.8 percent are casual labour, and only 5.5 percent are regular wage/salaried. Out of these 83.7 percent self-employed female workers, 39.8 percent are engaged as helpers in household enterprises. Note—The category of self-employed workers also includes those workers who had work in household enterprises but could not work due to illness or some other reason.

stem: At what percentage has Bihar registered the lowest Female Workforce Participation Rate for the year 2020- 2022?

options.label: a
options.text: 7% in rural and 9.1% in urban areas

options.label: b
options.text: 4% in rural and 6.5% in urban areas

options.label: c
options.text: 6% in rural and 8.1% in urban areas

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: According to the data released by the National Sample Survey Office (Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, Government of India), in 2020–21 and 2021–22, Bihar recorded the lowest female workforce participation rate (15 years and above) among all states of India. In 2020–21 and 2021–22, the female workforce participation rate in Bihar was, respectively, 11.2 percent and 10.1 percent in rural areas, and 6.3 percent and 10.5 percent in urban areas. According to the data for 2023–24, the female workforce participation rate in rural and urban areas is 33.1 percent and 15.5 percent, respectively. It is noteworthy that the Bihar Public Service Commission considered option (b) as the correct answer to this question.

stem: According to the National Family Health Survey-5 released by the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare on November 24, 2021, there has been a significant improvement in the sex ratio of Bihar. It has increased from_________in 2015-2016 to________in 2020-2022.

expl: In the National Family Health Survey (NFHS)-5 released by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, an improvement compared to the previous period is reflected in Bihar’s sex ratio. In Bihar, the sex ratio shown as 1062/1000 in the NFHS-4 (2015–16) survey has become 1090/1000 in NFHS- 5 (2019–21). Note— The mention of 2020–2022 in the given question is erroneous. stem: According to the Bihar Economic Survey (2021-2022), what was the rate of growth of Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) of Bihar in 2020-2021?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: According to the Bihar Economic Survey (2021–2022), due to the impact of COVID-19 and the lockdown, Bihar’s Gross State Domestic Product increased by only 2.5 percent in 2020–2021. According to the Bihar Economic Survey (2024–25), in 2023–24, Bihar’s per capita Gross State Domestic Product increased by 12.8 percent at current prices and by 7.6 percent at constant prices (2011–12) compared to the previous year.

stem: Which one of the following is correct for Bihar economy?

options.label: a
options.text: The occupational structure of the economy is stagnant from above.

options.label: b
options.text: The growth rate is one of the lowest in India at 2.5%.

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: The occupational structure of Bihar’s economy is stagnant in nature at the upper level. Bihar’s economy is mainly based on agriculture (the primary sector). According to the Bihar Economic Survey (2021–22), due to the impact of the lockdown, the growth rate of Bihar’s GSDP at current prices in 2020–21 was 2.5 percent (2.4 percent as per the Bihar Economic Survey, 2024–25), which was the lowest among all the states in India. According to the Bihar Economic Survey (2024–25), in 2023–24, Bihar’s Gross State Domestic Product growth rate compared to the previous year was estimated at 14.5 percent at current prices and 9.2 percent at constant prices (2011–12).

stem: According to the 15th Finance Commission’s recommendations, how much share will Bihar receive in divisible pool of Central pool of Central taxes from 2021-26?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: According to the recommendations of the 15th Finance Commission, from 2021–22 to 2025–26, Bihar will receive a 10.058 percent share from the divisible pool of central taxes and duties, which is the second highest among all states. The highest share among all states (17.939%) is received by Uttar Pradesh.

stem: Choose the incorrect statement as per the Economic Survey of Bihar, 2021-22.

options.label: b

expl: Established to ensure the social and economic empowerment of Bihar’s rural poor, the “Bihar Rural Livelihoods Project”, popularly known as “JEEViKA”, has achieved unprecedented success. It is primarily a State Government initiative related to poverty alleviation in rural areas of Bihar. Up to September, 2018, the estimated number of Self-Help Groups (SHGs) in Bihar was approximately 8.17 lakh. As per the Bihar Economic Survey 2024–25, under JEEViKA, up to September, 2024, 1063.5 thousand Self-Help Groups and 71.1 thousand Village Organizations were formed.

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: SPUR (Support Programme for Urban Reforms) is a six-year partnership programme of the Government of Bihar and the United Kingdom’s Department for International Development for supporting urban reforms in Bihar. Through the SPUR project, emphasis has been laid on economic growth and reduction of urban poverty by increasing the financial attractiveness for private investment in urban local body projects. The SPUR programme has five components— 1. Urban governance and planning 2. Municipal finance and accounting 3. Urban infrastructure 4. Local economic development 5. Social development, poverty alleviation and livelihoods.

expl: According to the Budget Speech 2022–23, sparsely populated border villages along the northern frontier, where connectivity and basic facilities are very limited and which have remained deprived of development benefits, will be covered under the Vibrant Village Programme. Activities under this programme include provision of basic village amenities, housing, construction of tourism centres, road connectivity, decentralized renewable energy arrangements, Direct-to-Home access for Doordarshan and educational channels, and support for livelihood generation. Additional funds will be provided for these activities.

options.text: Providing assets for sustainable income generation to the extremely poor families

options.label: d
options.text: Providing free training to enhance skills among youth

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The Government of Bihar launched the Sustainable Livelihood Scheme on 5 August, 2018. This scheme was started for extremely poor families, including those traditionally associated with the production, transportation and sale of country liquor and toddy (whose economic condition weakened after the implementation of prohibition in the State), as well as targeted extremely poor families from Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and other communities. This initiative aims to build self-confidence among identified families and develop entrepreneurial skills. After completion of training, each targeted family is allocated up to `2 lakh under the Livelihood Investment Fund.

expl: Under the aegis of the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, and the Government of Bihar, an Export Promotion Industrial Park (EPIP) has been established at Hajipur as a multi-product export-processing zone for North Bihar. It focuses on developing the high-level infrastructure required for export-oriented units.

stem: Which of the following is not true about Bihar's Mukhyamantri Kanya Utthan Yojana?

options.label: a
options.text: Proposed annual expenditure for the scheme is ` 7,221 crore

options.label: b
options.text: Education, Health and Social Welfare three departments run the scheme

options.label: c
options.text: Every girl child will receive total ` 60000 from her birth to graduation level education

options.label: d
options.text: At the time of a girl child's birth, her family receives ` 2000

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The Mukhyamantri Kanya Utthan Yojana, launched in April 2018 by Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar, is a major initiative of the Government of Bihar. Its objective is to promote girls’ education and empowerment by providing financial support from birth up to the graduate level. Initially, the Bihar Government allocated a budget of about Rs. 2,221 crore per year for implementation. It is an integrated scheme implemented jointly by multiple departments. The nodal department is the Social Welfare Department, which performs the main coordination role, while the other two departments— Education and Health—provide benefits at different stages. Under this scheme, a girl receives total financial assistance of Rs. 94,100 (in different instalments) from birth till graduation. Notably, earlier this amount was fixed at Rs. 54,100, which was enhanced with approval of the State Cabinet in February 2021. The scheme also provides Rs. 2,000 to the family at the time of the girl child’s birth.
